answer: Timber rule: pay each key in proportion to its graded work raised to the power 1.5, so reward is convex, not per-head. Split work W over N keys and the total is N(W/N)^1.5 = W^1.5/sqrt(N): a 1,000-key farm earns about 1/32 of one key doing the same work, so a willow of thin clones only loses. A flat equal-split pool is the plume sybils feed on; drop it. Risk: incumbents gain, so cap the curve at 100 epochs of decaying history and make history non-transferable.
